YMCA CAMPERS TO RE-TRACE FUR ROUTES 
SUBJECT/ SUJET 


WORD COUNT/ NOMBRE DE MOTS 150 


FOR/COMMUNIQUE AU NOM eS a rs ae ae a en a 


AT WILL 
FOR PUBLICATION/PUBLIABLE 


POUR RENSEIGNEMENTS 


ER AVE 
com MUNG ONTAGT WILLIAM SHER 


1; 
Seven 14-15 year old boys and two counsellors from the Montreal 
YMCA's Kamp Kanawana plan to re-trace 150 miles of Canada's original 


east-west fur trade route in canoes. 


The group will be moved by truck from Kanawana, in St. Sauveur, 
Que., to Deep River, Ont., on August 2. They will leave next day, 
via water, for Britannia Beach, Ottawa, which they expect to reach 


on August 9. 


The trip is part of a Centennial Project of the Canadian Camping 


Association. 


Continued 


2 6 
While en route to Ottawa, the boys will log their observations 
of wild life, water currents, camping facilities, weather conditions 


and land structure. 


This data, together with information assembled by groups from 
other camps on similar expeditions, will be assembled into a guide 


book. 


When the YMCA group arrives in Ottawa, it will be greeted by 200 
fellow campers from Kanawana who, after a chuckwagon lunch, will 


tour the Parliament Buildings.
